deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is a working page from Riemann's genus-3 (p=3) theory: theta functions with half-integer characteristics and their link to the 28 bitangents of a plane quartic. The context is the same as the posthumous 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3' material edited by Weber. Notation on the page: n is a base characteristic and p,q,r,d,e,f are half-periods. A symbol 'n+p' etc. names a characteristic. A bare factor (n+p) after a product of ϑ's denotes the vector of first partial derivatives at 0 of the odd theta function ϑ[n+p](v). That is the gradient (∂ϑ[n+p]/∂v_1, ∂ϑ[n+p]/∂v_2, ∂ϑ[n+p]/∂v_3)(0). Up to a linear change of coordinates it gives the coefficient vector of the corresponding bitangent.

(A) Bookkeeping tables (top of page). Riemann lists characteristics n+p, n+q, n+r; n+q+r, n+p+r, n+p+q; n+d, n+d+p, n+d+q, n+d+r; n+e, n+f; n+e+f+p+q+r etc. Beside them he places the matching bitangent forms: x, y, z; ξ, η, ζ; and the triple sums x+y+z, x+η+ζ, ξ+y+ζ, ξ+η+z. This is the dictionary between an Aronhold-type system of odd characteristics and the bitangent linear forms in Riemann's normal form of the quartic, √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0.

(B) Linear-form manipulation (middle). Riemann renames the six forms x,y,z,t,u,v with x+y+z+t+u+v=0. He considers the four triple sums x+y+z, x+u+v, t+y+v, t+u+z, and sets:
- η = t+y+v,
- ζ = t+u+z,
- −ξ = t+y+z (equivalently ξ = x+u+v).

He then rewrites a linear form of the type ξ/α+βy+γz, which belongs to Riemann's normal-form relation of the type αx+y/β+z/γ = −(ξ/α+βy+γz):
- Substituting −ξ = t+y+z gives −(ξ/α+βy+γz) = t/α + (1/α−β)y + (1/α−γ)z.
- This factors as (1/α)(1−αβ)(1−αγ)[ t/((1−αβ)(1−αγ)) + y/(1−αγ) + z/(1−αβ) ].
- A further rewriting is = −1/(1−βγ)·( αβγ x + (x+u+v)/α − γ(u+v) − β(u+v) ).

So he is expressing the 7th-bitangent-type forms in different bases of the Aronhold system.

(C) Jacobian determinant. The line Σ±(n+q)(n+r)(n+d) = ± ϑn·ϑ(n+q+r+d+e)·ϑ(n+q+r+d+f)·ϑ(n+q+r+d+p)·ϑ(n+p+e+f) is written with the leading 'ϑ(n+q+r+d)' struck out. Read as: the 3×3 determinant of the gradients of three odd theta functions equals (up to a constant, implicitly π^3, and sign) a product of g+2 = 5 even theta constants. This is the genus-3 instance of the Jacobian-Nullwert formula, the analogue of Jacobi's ϑ1' = π ϑ2ϑ3ϑ4 and of Rosenhain's genus-2 formula.

(D) Four-term linear relation. Four vectors (n+p),(n+q),(n+r),(n+d) in C^3 are linearly dependent. By Cramer/Laplace expansion, Σ_i ± D(jkl)·grad_i = 0, where D(jkl) is the determinant of the other three. My inference: each D is replaced by its 5-fold theta product (C). The common factor ϑn·ϑ(n+p+q+r+d) is then divided out; this is the same characteristic in all four terms if n+q+r+d+p is symmetric. What remains is Riemann's relation:
- ϑ(n+q+r+d+e)ϑ(n+q+r+d+f)ϑ(n+p+e+f)·(n+p)
- + ϑ(n+p+r+d+e)ϑ(n+p+r+d+f)ϑ(n+q+e+f)·(n+q)
- + ϑ(n+p+q+d+e)ϑ(n+p+q+d+f)ϑ(n+r+e+f)·(n+r)
- + ϑ(n+p+q+r+e)ϑ(n+p+q+r+f)ϑ(n+d+e+f)·(n+d) = 0,

signs absorbed into the characteristics. This is a linear relation among four bitangents with cubic theta-constant coefficients.

(E) Consistency checks. Riemann rederives coefficients with roles of d,e,f interchanged; for example ϑ(n+p+q+d+e)ϑ(n+p+q+e+f)ϑ(n+r+d+f)(n+r), with factors underlined for comparison. A dependence of 4 vectors in C^3 is unique up to a scalar (for generic position). So two derivations must give proportional coefficient sets. Comparing them (the two-row bracket for (n+q), and the (n+d) block) yields identities between products of five, resp. three, even theta constants. The last line is a two-term expression of this kind: −ϑ(n+p+d+e+f)ϑ(n+p+d+e+r)ϑ(q+r+f)(n+q) + ϑ(n+p+q+e+f)ϑ(n+p+q+e+r)ϑ(d+r+f)(n+d). The page breaks off without a final stated result.
errors: In the last line 'ϑ(q+r+f)' and 'ϑ(d+r+f)' lack the base characteristic n. By the pattern of every other factor these should be ϑ(n+q+r+f), ϑ(n+d+r+f). This is very probably a notational slip.
In the list 'n+q+p n+r+p n+r+p' the third entry should by the pattern be n+d+p (copying slip, by Riemann or the transcriber).

The final rewriting '= −1/(1−βγ)(αβγx + (x+u+v)/α − γ(u+v) − β(u+v))' is not an identity in the free variables. The coefficient of x on the right does not vanish while the left side has no x. It can only hold after using the normal-form relation (the incomplete 'αx+y/β+z/γ = …'), which is not written out. It is therefore unverified from the page.

The determinant formula omits the constant factor (π^3 for Riemann's normalization) and the sign. The struck-out ϑ(n+q+r+d) shows hesitation over which five constants occur. The page gives no derivation, only the statement.

results.what: Dictionary between odd theta characteristics (n+p, n+q, …, built from 7 half-periods) and bitangent forms x,y,z,ξ,η,ζ and their triple sums, with x+y+z+ξ+η+ζ=0 (Riemann normal form of the plane quartic)
results.modern_name: Aronhold system of bitangents / Riemann's normal form √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0 and its theta-characteristic labelling
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures, publ. posthumously; Weber 1876 'Theorie der Abelschen Functionen vom Geschlecht 3'); Aronhold 1864 for the 7-bitangent system

results.what: 3×3 determinant of gradients of three odd genus-3 theta functions at 0 equals ± a product of five even theta constants
results.modern_name: Jacobian Nullwert formula (generalized Jacobi derivative formula) in genus 3
results.usually_credited_to: Frobenius (1885), Thomae; Riemann–Weber for genus 3 bitangent relations; modern treatment Igusa (1980)

results.what: Four-term linear relation among gradients of four odd thetas (bitangent forms) with cubic theta-constant coefficients, obtained via Cramer expansion plus the Jacobian formula
results.modern_name: Linear relations among bitangents with theta-constant coefficients (Riemann–Weber moduli of the quartic)

results.what: Comparison of alternative coefficient expressions giving identities among products of even theta constants

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's genus-3 theta/bitangent theory is known from his posthumously published lectures and Weber's 1876 book, so the setting is expected. The somewhat notable point is the explicit statement that a 3×3 Jacobian of odd thetas equals a product of five even theta constants, used to produce bitangent linear relations. That genus-3 Jacobian-Nullwert formula is normally cited from Frobenius (1885)/Thomae. However, it is plausibly implicit in the Riemann–Weber material, and the page gives no proof.

checkable.asserts: The factorization on the page is an identity (result 0).

checkable.sympy: q=Rational(1,10); th=lambda f: N(f); from mpmath import jtheta, pi; abs(jtheta(1,0,q,1)-pi*jtheta(2,0,q)*jtheta(3,0,q)*jtheta(4,0,q)) < 1e-12
checkable.asserts: Genus-1 analogue (Jacobi): ϑ1'(0) = π ϑ2ϑ3ϑ4, the g=1 case of the Jacobian-Nullwert formula used for g=3 on the page (mpmath, derivative order 1).

transcription_corrections: In '−(x/α+βy+γz)' the first variable should be ξ, not x: −(ξ/α+βy+γz). Only with ξ = −(t+y+z) does the next equality hold.
'n+q+p n+r+p n+r+p' should read 'n+q+p n+r+p n+d+p' (pattern; the image appears to repeat r, possibly Riemann's own slip).
The leading struck-out factor in the determinant line is ϑ(n+q+r+d) (deleted), followed by ϑn; the transcription is correct to mark it deleted.
In the last line the factor '[?]' ϑ(n+p+d+e+r) is plausibly read as such; ϑ(q+r+f) and ϑ(d+r+f) are written without n in the image.
